page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 64 physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 AWS Graviton2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates one hardware thread per core with dedicated execution, eliminating hypervisor overhead. System memory comprises 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per physical core. For storage and networking, the platform bundles 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no hardware graphics accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate that the 64-core ARM architecture excels in highly parallel, multi-threaded execution while displaying weaker single-thread capabilities. Synthetic evaluation via stress-ng multi-core reaches 97,228.89, placing it in the top tier, whereas single-core stress-ng records 1,522.89 and single-core Geekbench scores 978.0. Real-world parallel tasks showcase strong compute and I/O efficiency: software compilation with Clang scores 43,553.0 and ray tracing hits 50,408.0. In memory and throughput profiling, cached reads register 3,791.56 GB/sec, Redis SET throughput achieves 73.41 million operations per second, and static web serving hits 46.63 GB/sec.

The hardware trades off single-threaded throughput and raw per-core vector capabilities—evidenced by weak single-core compression benchmarks—for massive core parallelism and dense NVMe disk bandwidth. Large language model inference speeds fall behind dedicated GPU architectures, yielding just 2.38 tokens per second on large 70B models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the ARM Neoverse architecture delivers high concurrent compute and caching density without virtualization penalties, making c6gd.metal well suited for high-concurrency web serving, large-scale CI/CD build farms, parallel distributed computing, and I/O-heavy caching tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton2 ARM Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM (2.0 GB per core), 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and 25 Gbps baseline networking, without dedicated GPUs. Multi-threaded benchmark measurements illustrate high parallel execution, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng score of 97,228.89, Clang software build score of 43,553.0, and 73.41 million Redis operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect the lower clock profile, with a Geekbench single-core score of 978.0. This bare-metal instance offers dense core capacity and fast local NVMe storage, making it suitable for high-throughput distributed caching, compilation pipelines, multi-threaded batch jobs, and large-scale web serving.
